title: RecordPage
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar, MonarchTabs and Tab, one scrolling section per tab, MonarchDescriptionList for the details and MonarchActivityTimeline (a lazy list) for the activity
summary: A recipe, not a component: a record's detail screen on a phone, with the name and actions in the top app bar, a status, section tabs, and the side column and the activity moved into their own tabs.
whenToUse: For the detail screen of a record (a deal, a contact, a ticket) reached from a list.
whenNotToUse: For the list and the record side by side on a tablet or a foldable, put this screen in the detail pane of NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold (split-layout). For the header alone, use the record-header recipe.
api: TopAppBar(title = { Text(name, maxLines = 1, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis) }, navigationIcon = …, actions = { … })
MonarchTabs(selectedIndex = currentTab, onSelectedIndexChange = { currentTab = it }) { sections.forEach { tab(it) } }

options.name: tabs
options.description: The sections of the record; add a Details tab for the web's side column and an Activity tab for the activity.

options.name: tab
options.description: The selected section, kept with rememberSaveable so it survives rotation.

options.name: actions
options.description: The record's actions in the top app bar; put the rest in an overflow MonarchMenu.

states.name: section
states.description: The selected tab's content fills the space under the tabs and scrolls on its own.

states.name: details
states.description: The web's side column: MonarchDescriptionList with the record's facts, in its own tab.

states.name: activity
states.description: MonarchActivityTimeline, a lazy list, fills the rest of the screen and scrolls on its own.

states.name: wide
states.description: On an expanded window, show the details beside the main column with split-layout instead of a tab.

appearance: Every part is an existing Material 3 or Monarch component: the top app bar and tabs in the Monarch theme, a status badge, a description list and the activity timeline. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships RecordPage as one component: a RecordHeader with tabs, the main column, an aside that moves under the main column below a breakpoint, and an activity section. On a phone Android follows the native pattern instead of copying the web layout: the name and actions go to the TopAppBar (as in the record-header recipe), the side column becomes a Details tab, and the activity is its own tab, because MonarchActivityTimeline is a lazy list that must not sit inside a vertically scrolling parent. iOS keeps the side column under the main column with ViewThatFits and the activity as a tab; it also mentions a Details tab as the other phone choice. On wide windows use NavigableSupportingPaneScaffold or the split-layout entry rather than a breakpoint. The web's asideWidth and activityPlacement props are choices in the recipe's own code.
accessibility: The record's name is the top app bar title; actions are buttons with 48dp targets.
Tabs have the tab role and the selected state, from Material 3.
The status is a word in a MonarchStatusBadge, not color alone.
Each section scrolls on its own, so TalkBack scrolls the content under the fixed header and tabs.
edgeCases: A long record name is cut with an ellipsis in the app bar; show it in full in the Overview section.
Many sections: MonarchTabs scrolls the tabs.
Never put MonarchActivityTimeline inside verticalScroll; give it the remaining height with weight(1f).
